If you are a resident of Lake County or have ever had a legal issue in the area, you may have heard of the Lake County Circuit Court. In this article, we will provide a comprehensive guide to the Lake County Circuit Court, including its history, structure, and the types of cases it handles.

History of the Lake County Circuit Court

The Lake County Circuit Court has a long and rich history, dating back to its establishment in 1843. The court was initially established as a county court, with jurisdiction over all legal matters within the county. Over time, the court's jurisdiction expanded, and it became known as the Lake County Circuit Court.

In the early years, the court was held in various locations throughout the county, including schools, churches, and other public buildings. In 1895, the first courthouse was built in Waukegan, the county seat of Lake County. This courthouse served the county for over 70 years, until it was replaced by a new courthouse in 1967.

Structure of the Lake County Circuit Court

The Lake County Circuit Court is divided into several divisions, each of which is responsible for handling specific types of cases. The main divisions of the court include:

Criminal Division

The Criminal Division of the Lake County Circuit Court is responsible for handling all criminal cases filed within the county. This includes felony cases, misdemeanor cases, and traffic cases. The division is also responsible for overseeing the county's drug court program.

Civil Division

The Civil Division of the Lake County Circuit Court handles all civil cases filed within the county. This includes cases involving contracts, personal injury, property disputes, and more. The division is also responsible for overseeing the county's small claims court.

Family Division

The Family Division of the Lake County Circuit Court handles all family law matters filed within the county. This includes divorce, child custody, child support, and other related matters.

Juvenile Division

The Juvenile Division of the Lake County Circuit Court handles all cases involving minors. This includes delinquency cases, abuse and neglect cases, and other related matters.

Types of Cases Handled by the Lake County Circuit Court

As previously mentioned, the Lake County Circuit Court is responsible for handling a variety of legal matters. Some of the most common types of cases handled by the court include:

Criminal Cases

Criminal cases are those in which an individual is accused of committing a crime. These cases can range from minor traffic violations to serious felony offenses. The Lake County Circuit Court is responsible for handling all criminal cases filed within the county.

Civil Cases

Civil cases are those in which one party is suing another party for damages. These cases can involve a variety of legal issues, including breach of contract, personal injury, property disputes, and more.

Family Law Cases

Family law cases are those in which legal issues arise within a family. These cases can involve divorce, child custody, child support, and other related matters.

Juvenile Cases

Juvenile cases are those in which minors are involved. These cases can include delinquency cases, abuse and neglect cases, and other related matters.

The Lake County Circuit Court plays a crucial role in the legal system of Lake County. It is responsible for handling a wide variety of legal matters, from criminal cases to family law matters. FAQs

How do I file a case with the Lake County Circuit Court?

You can file a case with the Lake County Circuit Court by visiting the courthouse

What are the operating hours of the Lake County Circuit Court?

The Lake County Circuit Court is open from 8:30 am to 5:00 pm, Monday through Friday, except for court holidays.

How do I find out about the status of my case?

You can check the status of your case by contacting the Clerk of the Circuit Court's office or by accessing the court's online case search tool.

Can I represent myself in court?

Yes, you have the right to represent yourself in court, but it is recommended that you seek the advice of an attorney, especially in complex legal matters.

What should I expect during a court hearing?

During a court hearing, the judge will hear arguments from both sides and make a decision based on the evidence presented. It is important to be respectful and follow the court's rules and procedures.
